title: Secret Sauce simulation dish
description: One authored dish in the simulation LIBRARY. Identical to recipeData/schema.json except for two keys: `demo` is rejected (engagement is generated from a modelled history, never authored) and `sim` is allowed (generation hints). Every other field means exactly what it means there, and both directories are validated by the same code — tool/recipe_format.dart — so a dish can be promoted into the curated set by moving the file and deleting its `sim` block. Neither schema file is read at runtime (no JSON Schema dependency in the toolchain), so a rule added here must be added to tool/recipe_format.dart or tool/sim.dart as well. Directory-level rules (category/cuisine coverage) are not expressible in JSON Schema at all and live in tool/sim.dart — see simData/README.md.

demo.description: REJECTED here. A hand-typed like_count is the exact practice Phase 24 replaces: supabase/sim/2_sim_generate.sql writes the engagement ROWS and lets the same arithmetic the triggers use derive the counters. Put a dish's expected popularity in `sim.weight` instead.

sim.description: Generation hints. Optional, and so are both of its fields.

weight.description: Relative likelihood the generator draws this dish. Raise it for everyday food, lower it for a project bake — a library where a three-hour paella is as common as a weeknight curry does not produce a Discover page that looks real.

variant_titles.description: Title templates, used so one dish can become several recipes without colliding. `(owner_id, title)` is the import key and a collision silently collapses two recipes into one row (SDS §11.2), so the generator needs distinct titles per owner. Generic fallbacks apply when a dish supplies none.

items.description: Must contain the literal `{title}` — it is a template, not a title.
